newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-CADDIES ALLOWED TO WEAR SHORTS AT THIS YEAR'S U.S. OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CADDIES ALLOWED TO WEAR SHORTS AT THIS YEAR'S U.S. OPEN.

text.p: Spectators at this week's U.S. Open at Congressional Country Club will see sights never before seen at the national golf championship -- the bare legs of the caddies.

Concerned about the sweltering heat and humidity that made the 1964 Open staged here a survival test for participants, the U.S. Golf Association has made a radical fashion statement by allowing caddies to wear shorts for the first time in this 97th edition of the tournament.
"We are providing a more comfortable work place environment," USGA executive director David Fay said on the eve of Thursday's opening round. "I mean, it is hard work lugging that big bag around."
The players, who merely swing the clubs, are still required to wear trousers.
